Coefficients at all t^(2m) have strictly nonnegative polynomial dependence on δ=6T²/S³. The radial chi-three factor and L2 normalization give the displayed constants. The cubic discriminant gives the exact feasible δ interval, with correct endpoint eigenvalue classifications. The L^m triangle inequality gives the complex upper bound; equality requires proportional real quadratics, hence only complex scalar zonal cases. The sextic constants and deficit follow algebraically. Embedded exact rational checker passed 291 assertions but is supplemental; no finite experiment substitutes for the analytic all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text overlap establishes only the fourth moment of the same degree-two space and specifically describes its shape independence on S^2. The new all-even higher-moment polynomial, sharp sixth-moment anisotropy gap, biaxial lower extremizers and complex upper rigidity are not implied by that fourth-moment theorem. Examined original-text projection and Nikolskii articles are degree-asymptotic and not exact finite-degree-two classifications. A classical Gaussian moment series is a method but does not itself classify the sharp extremizers. Priority is best-knowledge, not independently certified.

value.rationale: Pure degree-two harmonics on S² have a previously established shape-degenerate sharp quartic norm. The normalized sixth moment is the first natural higher norm to distinguish uniaxial and biaxial shapes, with a global exact deficit of size 1000(1-δ)/1001. The finding determines sharp real upper and lower bounds for every even order, a positive invariant polynomial and complete equality orbits, and extends upper rigidity to complex harmonics. This resolves a natural infinite family of spectral eigenfunction norm comparisons rather than merely tabulating values or rephrasing prior quartic results. Higher degree and non-even exponent questions are not claimed.
